historical_claims.source_locator: Composition and the poem’s three broad narrative modes

historical_claims.anchor: The earliest rulers appear in a world
historical_claims.source_locator: Opening, Keyumars, Hushang, Tahmuras and Jamshid cycles

historical_claims.anchor: The story of Zahhak gives bad kingship a bodily image
historical_claims.source_locator: Zahhak and Fereydun: serpents, Kaveh, overthrow and binding

historical_claims.anchor: Fereydun divides his dominion among three sons
historical_claims.source_locator: Fereydun cycle and the legendary framework of Iran/Turan, not modern borders

historical_claims.anchor: Zal is born with white hair
historical_claims.source_locator: Manuchehr cycle: Sam, Zal, Simorgh, Rudabeh and Rostam’s birth

historical_claims.anchor: During an adventure in Samangan, Rostam meets Tahmineh
historical_claims.source_locator: Sohrab cycle: union, token, manipulation, encounters and recognition

historical_claims.anchor: Siyavash, a prince educated under Rostam's care
historical_claims.source_locator: Siyavash cycle: Sudabeh, fire, exile, Farangis and murder
Great war with Afrasiyab and the end of Kay Khosrow’s reign

historical_claims.anchor: Ferdowsi also preserves verse associated with the earlier poet Daqiqi
historical_claims.source_locator: Goshtasp cycle: embedded earlier verse and religious narrative

historical_claims.anchor: At last he is sent to bring Rostam to court in bonds
historical_claims.source_locator: Rostam and Esfandiyar cycle: command, duel, Simorgh and Bahman

historical_claims.anchor: His half-brother Shaghad arranges a trap
historical_claims.source_locator: Rostam and Shaghad, followed by Bahman’s reign

historical_claims.anchor: The sequence moves through Dara to Eskandar
historical_claims.source_locator: Dara and Eskandar cycles: dynastic construction and Alexander romance

historical_claims.anchor: After the Arsacid rulers, the poem reaches the Sasanian line
historical_claims.source_locator: Arsacid and Ardashir cycles; historical setting is distinct from narrated adventures

historical_claims.anchor: In the story of Borzuya's journey to India
historical_claims.source_locator: Khosrow Anushirvan cycle and literary transmission of Kalila wa Dimna
Yazdegerd cycle, the conquest setting, and the distinction between the two Rostams

transcript.scope: Original compact narrative and interpretation; no modern translation reproduced.

composition.note: 003000 opening and claim 003000-c01 explicitly date Ferdowsi’s completion around 1010, not the legendary events narrated.
composition.label: c. 1010

description: Retells major episodes of Ferdowsi’s Shahnameh, from legendary kings to Rostam and Sohrab and later dynastic conflict, examining heroism, inheritance, and political loss.
